He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball|UNC Asheville Bulldogs]] and the [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor Bears]]. ==High school career== As a sophomore at [[Summit Country Day School]] in [[Cincinnati|Cincinnati, Ohio]], Teague averaged 14.2 points per game. For his junior season, he transferred to [[Walnut Hills High School]] in Cincinnati, where he averaged 22.4 points per game in his first year.{{cite web |last1=Springer |first1=Scott |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2020/01/24/ex-walnut-hills-guard-macio-teague-top-threat-baylor-basketball/4547591002/ |title=Former Walnut Hills great MaCio Teague now a big key for top-ranked No. 1 Baylor |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=July 15, 2020 |date=January 24, 2020}} On January 19, 2015, as a senior, Teague scored a school-record 51 points in a 96–48 win over [[Piqua High School]] at the Flyin' to the Hoop Invitational. He scored the second-most single-game points in the event's history, behind only [[Byron Mullens]].{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=MaCio Teague's 51 lift Walnut Hills at Flyin' to the Hoop |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2015/01/19/macio-teague-lifts-walnut-hills-past-piqua/22001821/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=July 15, 2020 |date=January 19, 2015}} Teague finished the season averaging 26.4 points and 7.5 rebounds per game, leading the Ohio Division I in scoring. He was named [[Eastern Cincinnati Conference]] and District 16 Player of the Year, while earning Second Team All-State honors.{{cite web |title=MaCio Teague |url=https://baylorbears.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/macio-teague/9734 |publisher=Baylor University Athletics |accessdate=July 15, 2020}} Teague played a [[postgraduate season]] at [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]] to further develop and to gain more exposure.{{cite web |last1=Turer |first1=Adam |title=Catching up: Sky's the limit for Walnut Hills product MaCio Teague at UNC Asheville |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/high-school-sports/2018/02/15/catching-up-skys-limit-walnut-hills-product-macio-teague-unc-asheville/341323002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=July 15, 2020 |date=February 15, 2018}}{{cite news |last1=Copeland |first1=Kareem |title=Baylor's small-school transfers have gone from bus rides and open gyms to No. 1 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/02/07/baylor-basketball-rises-with-transfers-freddie-gillespie-macio-teague/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=July 15, 2020 |date=February 7, 2020}} ==College career== ===UNC Asheville=== On February 11, 2017, Teague scored a freshman season-high 30 points for [[UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball|UNC Asheville]] in a 91–69 win over [[Longwood Lancers men's basketball|Longwood]].{{cite web |title=Teague hits 6 3s, UNC Asheville rolls past Longwood 91–69 |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/43159628/teague-hits-6-3s-unc-asheville-rolls-past-longwood-91-69 |website=[[KSL-TV]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=February 11, 2017}} As a freshman, he averaged 15.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game and was named [[Big South Conference|Big South]] Freshman of the Year while earning First Team All-Big South honors.{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=MaCio Teague named Big South Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2017/02/28/macio-teague-named-big-south-freshman-year/98519208/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=February 28, 2017}} Teague became the seventh player in conference history to record at least 500 points in his freshman season.{{cite web |title=UNC Asheville's MaCio Teague Listed Among Top 25 Sophomores by ESPN |url=https://bigsouthsports.com/news/2017/10/27/MBB_1027172644.aspx |publisher=[[Big South Conference]] |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=October 27, 2017}} On February 1, 2018, he scored a career-high 36 points and made seven three-pointers in a 64–57 victory over [[Campbell Fighting Camels basketball|Campbell]].{{cite web |title=Teague's Career Day Leads Bulldogs to League Road Win at Campbell |url=https://uncabulldogs.com/news/2018/2/1/mens-basketball-teagues-career-day-leads-bulldogs-to-league-road-win-at-campbell.aspx |publisher=UNC Asheville Athletics |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=February 1, 2018}} As a sophomore, Teague averaged 16.7 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.6 steals per game, leading the Big South by shooting 42.5 percent from three-point range. He was named to the First Team All-Big South for his second consecutive year. After the season, he received his release to transfer from UNC Asheville.{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=Report: Ex-Walnut Hills star MaCio Teague considers Xavier, Louisville |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/04/11/ex-walnut-hills-star-macio-teague-receives-release-transfer-per-report/508168002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=April 11, 2018}} ===Baylor=== On April 30, 2018, Teague announced that he would continue his college career with [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] over offers from [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{cite web |last1=Seymour |first1=Mark |title=Baylor Lands Talented Transfer MaCio Teague |url=https://www.ourdailybears.com/baylor-basketball/2018/4/30/17304044/baylor-lands-talented-transfer-macio-teague |publisher=Our Daily Bears |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=April 30, 2018}} He sat out the following season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] transfer rules and was a member of the team's practice squad. He made his debut for Baylor on November 5, 2019, scoring 18 points and collecting 10 rebounds in a 105–61 win over [[Central Arkansas Bears men's basketball|Central Arkansas]].{{cite news |title=Butler's 30 points lead No. 16 Baylor to 105–61 win over UCA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169593 |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} On February 8, 2020, Teague scored a junior season-high 24 points, including six straight free throws in the final 14 seconds, in a 78–70 win over [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]].{{cite web |title=No. 1 Baylor 7870 over Oklahoma State for 20th win in row |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169736 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=February 8, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 13.9 points and 4.6 rebounds in a team-high 32.6 minutes per game, helping Baylor achieve a 26–4 record.{{cite web |last1=Canizales |first1=Nick |title=MaCio Teague withdraws name from NBA Draft, will return to Baylor |url=https://www.kcentv.com/article/sports/macio-teague-withdraws-name-from-nba-draft-will-return-to-baylor/500-4bb4057a-8538-43b1-bc24-af05f14588bc |website=[[KCEN-TV]] |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=July 29, 2020}} Teague was named to the Second Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] and was a unanimous Big 12 All-Newcomer Team selection.{{cite web |title=MBB Racks Up Big 12 Yearly Awards |url=https://baylorbears.com/news/2020/3/8/mens-basketball-mbb-racks-up-big-12-yearly-awards.aspx |publisher=Baylor University Athletics |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |date=March 8, 2020}} After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], before withdrawing and returning to Baylor. On March 7, 2021, Teague scored 35 points, shooting 10-of-12 from three-point range, in an 88–73 win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]]. His 10 three-pointers tied for the most in program history and the second-most in Big 12 history.{{cite web |title=MBB's Teague Picks Up Player of the Week Honors |url=https://baylorbears.com/news/2021/3/8/mens-basketball-mbbs-teague-picks-up-player-of-the-week-honors.aspx |website=Baylor University Athletics |access-date=March 8, 2021 |date=March 8, 2021}} Baylor entered the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]] with a 1-seed and went on to win the national championship, finishing with a 28–2 record. In the tournament, Teague averaged nearly 15 points per game, including 22 points in the opening round against [[2021–22 Hartford Hawks men's basketball team|Hartford]] and the regional final against [[2021–22 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]], both of which led the team, and 19 points in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game victory]] over [[2021–22 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]]. He averaged 15.9 points and 4.0 rebounds per game on the season.{{cite web |title=MaCio Teague 2020–21 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/macio-teague-1/gamelog/2021 |access-date=October 5, 2022}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Teague signed with the [[Utah Jazz]] on August 15, 2021.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz sign MaCio Teague|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-macio-teague|website=NBA.com|date=August 15, 2021|access-date=August 16, 2021}} He was waived prior to the start of the season. In October 2021, Teague joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Training Camp Roster Finalized|url=https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/stars-finalize-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 1, 2021|archive-date=November 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102002429/https://saltlakecity.gleague.nba.com/stars-finalize-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} However, he was waived on March 22, 2022, after suffering a season-ending injury.{{cite web|title=2021–2022 Salt Lake City Stars Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Salt-Lake-City-Stars/42/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 29, 2022}} On July 29, 2022, Teague signed a contract with [[Baskets Oldenburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite web|title=MaCio Teague komplettiert Oldenburger Kader|url=https://ewe-baskets.de/news/verpflichtung-macio-teague.html|website=ewe-baskets.de|access-date=July 31, 2022}} On August 1, 2023, he signed with [[Czarni Słupsk]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Poland/news/821859/Macio-Teague-(ex-Oldenburg)-signs-at-Czarni|title=Macio Teague (ex Oldenburg) signs at Czarni|last=|first=|date=August 1, 2023|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=en|access-date=September 23, 2023}} On February 10, 2025, he signed with [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).{{Cite web|url=https://plk.pl/aktualnosci/25470/nowi-zawodnicy-we-wroclawiu|title=Nowi zawodnicy we Wrocławiu|last=|first=|date=February 10,
